title: What in your classroom has a count of four or five digits?
description: Kavya looks around her classroom for big counts. The video shows pages in the class notebooks and words in a storybook, and says other reasoned answers are fine.
teaching_notes: One idea: a 4 digit count starts at one thousand and a 5 digit count at ten thousand, so look for many small parts. Watch for children who pick a count like forty desks.

video_script.why: The child must find real counts in the classroom with four and five digits, and different children will find different ones.
video_script.substitution: Look for a small part, such as one notebook, then multiply by the number of parts.
video_script.anchor: Kavya looking around her classroom in Bengaluru
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu says forty desks is a four digit count. Forty has only two digits; a four digit number starts at one thousand.
video_script.payoff_line: one hundred pages of one hundred and twenty words make twelve thousand words

final_answer.value: Sample answer: pages in notebooks, 4,000 (4-digit); words in a storybook, 12,000 (5-digit)
final_answer.spoken: for example four thousand pages in the notebooks and twelve thousand words in a storybook, and other reasoned answers are fine

hold_back: Sample answer: pages in notebooks, 4,000 (4-digit); words in a storybook, 12,000 (5-digit)
never_show: forty desks marked as a 4 digit count
maths_rules: a 4 digit number is from 1,000 to 9,999; a 5 digit number is from 10,000 to 99,999
(i) 40 notebooks, about 100 pages each: 40 × 100 = 4,000 pages; 4 digits
(ii) a storybook of about 100 pages, about 120 words on each: 100 × 120 = 12,000 words; 5 digits
other answers are fine when the child can name the part and the number of parts
video_script.design: One idea: look for many small parts. Wrong idea: a count of forty is a four digit number. The classroom stays in the anchor band; the two samples build on the stage. Open prompt: other reasoned answers are fine.
